ev.help.entry: The limit or market entry from the signal.
ev.help.sl: Distance you can lose. 1 pip = pip size in price.
ev.help.win: Use the provider's real track record (the trade log), not a guess.
ev.help.spread: Paid on entry; counted as a cost on every trade.
ev.formula: How EV is computed. Expected value (EV) per trade = win rate × (reward − costs) − (1 − win rate) × (risk + costs). Break-even win rate = (risk + costs) ÷ (risk + reward). R means multiples of the risk on one trade.

ev.split.title: TP split: one target or several?
ev.split.intro: Enter up to 3 take-profit levels in pips (leave blank to skip). Probability is the chance of reaching that level given the previous level was reached, before the stop. The stop is not moved. "Split" opens one position per level with the lots divided equally.
ev.disclaimer: Illustrative only. The win rate must come from the signal provider's real, verified track record (see the dashboard's trade log); past results do not guarantee future ones. Costs here are estimates (slippage and swaps ignored). This is not financial advice.

page.hero.title: From chat message to order
page.hero.sub: How a signal posted in a WhatsApp chat or Telegram channel becomes a buy or sell order on your cTrader account, and every check it has to pass on the way.
page.hero.note: Timings are typical, not guaranteed. Automation ships switched off and in dry-run mode: nothing is traded until you turn it on.
page.flow.title: The path of one message
page.flow.lede: A message only becomes an order if it survives every step. Anything that fails stops there and is logged with the reason.
page.d.title: How a chat message becomes a cTrader order
page.d.descH: WhatsApp and Telegram messages reach the bridge. The bridge sends them to the Worker, which keeps only the chosen chat and queues them. Clairic extracts the trade, safety checks decide, and passing signals go to the cTrader Open API and IC Markets. Failing signals are ignored, rejected or recorded as a dry run. Every step is logged in D1 and shown on the dashboard.
page.d.descV: Top to bottom: WhatsApp and Telegram, bridge, Worker with target-chat filter, queue, Clairic extraction, safety checks, cTrader API, IC Markets. Safety checks that fail end as Ignored, Rejected or Dry run. Queue steps are logged in D1 and shown on the dashboard.
page.d.caption: Solid arrows are the trade path. Dashed arrows are the log lane: every message and order is written to D1 and shown on the dashboard. Safety checks end in one of four outcomes: order placed, Ignored, Rejected or Dry run.
page.stages.title: Five stages, in order
page.s1.p: One small program, the bridge, runs on a VPS or home server and listens to both WhatsApp and Telegram. It forwards messages from only the one chat you picked for each source.
page.s1.l1: WhatsApp: uses Baileys, which signs in like WhatsApp Web (you scan a QR code).
page.s1.l2: Telegram: signs in as your own user account over MTProto (GramJS), so it can read channels and groups you have joined. It may ask for your 2FA password.
page.s1.l3: Polling: the bridge asks the Worker for its instructions every 3 seconds: which accounts should be connected and which chat is the target.
page.s1.l4: Filtering: messages from any other chat are dropped, and empty messages (no text) are skipped.
page.s2.p: The bridge posts each message to the Worker. The Worker double-checks the chat, queues the message, and processes messages one at a time.
page.s2.l2: Target-chat check: the chat id must match the target chosen for that source (WhatsApp or Telegram). Otherwise the answer is "ignored".
page.s2.l3: Queue: accepted messages go into a Cloudflare Queue. The consumer handles one message at a time and has no short time limit, so extraction plus a broker session can finish.
page.s2.l4: Duplicates: each message id is stored once. If the same id arrives again it is ignored.
page.s3.p: An AI model on Cloudflare Workers AI (Clairic) reads the text and fills in a fixed set of fields, each with a confidence score. It reads; it does not invent.
page.s3.l1: Fields: action (BUY/SELL, LONG and SHORT count), order type (limit, stop, now, market), symbol, entry price (and upper end of a range), stop loss price, stop loss in pips, take-profit prices, take-profit pips, lot size, and entry time window (start and end).
page.s3.l2: Normalising: LONG becomes BUY and SHORT becomes SELL. Times like 20.10 become 20:10.
page.s3.l3: Pending orders: a limit or stop order without an entry price stays pending, so it is rejected later. It is never turned into a market order.
page.s3.l4: Every number must appear in the message. A price the model returns that is not written in the text is dropped, and the signal is rejected as a misread.
page.s3.l5: Pips need a unit. A pip value is only accepted when written next to "pips", "points" or "pts". A pip value echoed into a price field is discarded.
page.s3.l6: Is it a signal? Only if a side and a symbol are found (see the default symbol below). Confidence is the lower of the side and symbol scores.
page.s4.p: Plain code, not AI, decides whether the extracted trade is allowed. This is where most bad messages are stopped. The full list is in the safety rules table.
page.s4.l1: Symbol: if the message names none, your default symbol is used. Aliases are mapped (GOLD to XAUUSD), checked against an allow-list, and your broker suffix is added.
page.s4.l2: Pips to prices: pip distances are converted using a per-symbol pip size (gold is 0.1, so 25 pips is 2.5). This needs an entry price.
page.s4.l3: Time window: a window like 20.10-23.20 is read in your account timezone and becomes the pending order's expiry. A window that has already passed is rejected.
page.s4.l4: Sanity: confidence threshold, stop loss required, SL and TP on the correct side of entry, TP on the profit side of SL, messages older than 5 minutes ignored, max open positions.
page.s4.l5: Sizing: lot is fixed, or taken from the signal, capped at your max lot and rounded to 0.01. Take-profit strategy: first, last, or split into one position per TP with the lot divided evenly.
page.s4.l6: Dry run: if on, a valid trade is built and logged but never sent.
page.s5.p: The Worker opens a JSON WebSocket to cTrader's Open API, finds the symbol, converts lots to volume, and sends the order to your IC Markets account.
page.s5.l1: Connection: wss://demo.ctraderapi.com:5036 or live.ctraderapi.com:5036, authorised with an OAuth token that refreshes automatically.
page.s5.l2: Market orders: cTrader does not accept absolute SL/TP on market orders. So the Worker takes a spot quote (ask for BUY, bid for SELL), sends relative SL/TP, waits for the fill, then amends the position to the exact SL/TP prices.
page.s5.l3: Limit and stop orders: sent with absolute SL/TP. If there is an entry window, the order is good till date and expires at the end of it.
page.s5.l4: Record: each order request and response is stored in D1 and shown in the dashboard, including failures. Status ends as executed, partial or failed.

page.safety.title: Safety rules
page.safety.lede: These run on every signal before any order is sent. Most are settings you control in the dashboard.
page.r.1.p: Any trade when you have not turned automation on. Off by default.
page.r.2.p: Real orders while you are still testing. Orders are built and logged only.
page.r.3.p: Trading on messages from chats you did not choose.
page.r.4.p: The same message being traded twice.
page.r.5.p: Old messages replayed after a reconnect.
page.r.6.n: Numbers must be in the text
page.r.7.p: A price mistaken for a pip distance.
page.r.8.p: A limit or stop order silently becoming a market order.
page.r.10.p: Trades with no downside limit (default on).
page.r.11.p: SL or TP on the wrong side of entry, or TP below SL on a buy.
page.r.12.p: Entering after a stated time window has passed. Pending orders expire at its end.
page.r.13.p: Trading instruments you did not approve.
page.r.14.p: Stacking more exposure than you intend.

page.ev.title: Expected value: is a strategy worth following?
page.ev.intro: Expected value (EV) is what a strategy earns on average per trade after costs. A high win rate means nothing by itself: winning 80% of trades still loses money if the average loss is much bigger than the average win. What matters is the win rate together with the risk-to-reward ratio. Try your own numbers below.
page.gl.title: Glossary
page.gl.sl.d: A price at which the trade closes automatically to cap your loss.
page.gl.tp.d: A price at which the trade closes automatically to lock in a gain.
page.gl.lot.d: The trade size. 0.01 lot is the smallest step here; what a lot is worth depends on the instrument.
page.gl.pip.d: A small price unit. Its size depends on the instrument: 0.0001 for most pairs, 0.01 for JPY pairs, 0.1 for gold in this setup.
page.gl.r.d: Profit or loss measured in units of your initial risk. Risk 25 pips and make 50: that is +2R.
page.gl.spread.d: The gap between the buy price (ask) and sell price (bid). It is a cost on every trade; buys fill at the ask, sells at the bid.
page.gl.market.d: Fills now at the current price.
page.gl.limit.d: Waits for a better price: buy below the market or sell above it.
page.gl.stop.d: Waits for the price to move through a level: buy above the market or sell below it.
page.gl.gtd.d: Good till date: a pending order is cancelled automatically at a set time, here the end of the entry window.
page.foot.risk: Risk disclaimer. Trading leveraged products such as forex and CFDs carries a high risk of losing more than you can afford. Automation can fail or misread a message, and a fast order can still fill at a worse price. Examples on this page are illustrative. Nothing here is financial advice.
